native_result.query: In which years were individuals with a criminal record found to have significantly lower wealth compared to those without?
native_result.HypoA: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
native_result.HypoB: Individuals with a criminal record (jailed at some point between 1985-1994) had significantly lower wealth than those without in all three measured years: 1985, 1990, and 1996.
native_result.WorkflowB: Two-sided Mann-Whitney U per year (1985, 1990, 1996) comparing ever_jailed=1 vs 0 on composite wealth, retaining negatives and zeros; Bonferroni correction over 3 years (alpha per test ~0.0167); 'significantly lower' = adjusted p<0.05 with lower median and mean in the jailed group. Welch t and robustness regressions (rank and raw wealth ~ ever_jailed + race + sex) reported as complements only.

sub_hypo.text: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
sub_hypo.context: Participants in the National Longitudinal Study of Youth's 1979 cohort, with wealth measured in 1985, 1990, and 1996.
sub_hypo.relations: Individuals jailed between 1985 and 1994 (ever_jailed = 1) have significantly lower composite wealth in each of 1985, 1990, and 1996 than those not jailed during that period (ever_jailed = 0).

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.

sub_hypo.text: Individuals jailed at some point between 1985 and 1994 had significantly lower wealth than those not jailed during that period in each of 1985, 1990, and 1996.
sub_hypo.context: Participants in the National Longitudinal Study of Youth's 1979 cohort, comparing composite wealth in 1985, 1990, and 1996; negative and zero wealth values are retained.
sub_hypo.relations: In each measured year, ever_jailed=1 is associated with lower median and mean composite wealth than ever_jailed=0, with a two-sided Mann-Whitney U Bonferroni-adjusted p<0.05 across three yearly tests (per-test alpha approximately 0.0167). Welch t tests and regressions of rank and raw wealth on ever_jailed, adjusting for race and sex, are complementary analyses only.

gen_sub_hypo.full_hypo: Individuals with a criminal record (jailed at some point between 1985-1994) had significantly lower wealth than those without in all three measured years: 1985, 1990, and 1996.
